prerequisites: EM1012 - Mecànica de Màquines i Estructures
EM1015 - Ciència i Tecnologia de Materials
EM1019 - Elasticitat i Resistència de Materials
EM1020 - Teoria de Màquines i Mecanismes

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the ability to write and defend a team project in the field of thermal machines and installations.
Know how to solve problems related to combustion, furnaces, boilers, thermal machines and engines.
Be able to solve, analyze and apply thermodynamic cycles.
Be able to differentiate, explain and analyze the equipment where combustion processes are utilized.
Be able to calculate, explain and classify the different combustion processes.
Know how to differentiate, explain and analyze the different thermal machines and engines.
Know how to apply different thermal machines and engines in industrial processes, differentiating their advantages and disadvantages.
Know the current regulations related to thermal machines and installations.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Properties of thermal machine fluids.
Topic 2. Energy and the first principle of thermodynamics
Topic 3. Second principle of thermodynamics and reference cycles
Topic 7. Refrigeration and compression heat pump cycles
teaching_methods: Lectures (exposing theoretical content and main characteristics of thermodynamic cycles, multimedia presentations, blackboard, virtual sessions via Google Meet).
Exercise and problem solving (studying and solving problems on blackboard, multimedia support, problems available beforehand).
Problem-based learning (for problem-solving sessions and individual deliverable exercises, autonomous resolution, submission via Virtual Classroom).
Case study (working with diagrams and data of representative thermal installations for specific thermodynamic cycles).

Laboratory work (practical teaching sessions, autonomous programming of thermodynamic cycles using EES software in computer lab, studying influence of operating parameters, drafting final report for Virtual Classroom; experimental measurements in laboratory sessions to analyze thermodynamic cycles, virtual lab sessions via Google Meet, collaborative applications like Google Drive).

assessment_methods.method: Three problems to be solved during the course

assessment_rules: To pass, a minimum of 5 out of 10 points is required for the overall grade. In the first call, continuous evaluation contributes 30% (lab work 15%, three problems 15%), and the exam contributes 70% (first semester exam 10%, second semester final exam 60%). The second semester final exam requires a "PASSED" grade on a theoretical concepts test for the practical problem-solving part to count, and a minimum of 4 out of 10 for the final exam grade. In the second call, continuous evaluation from lab work (15%) is not recoverable, and the final exam (70% for main content + 15% for deliverable exercises) requires a minimum of 4 out of 10. For the extraordinary end-of-studies call, the exam accounts for 100% of the final grade, including a pass/fail test and problem-solving.
